# Inferra

Deploy apps from GitHub. Website: https://inferralab.com/
API and CLI default: https://api.inferralab.com

## Configuration v3
- inferra init writes v3: .inferra/repo.yaml, the app folder's .inferra/app.yaml and an optional GitHub environment-sync workflow. It does not write account.yaml.
- repo.yaml comes from the default branch and selects branches, repo teams, shared env and branch quotas. app.yaml comes from the deployed branch and defines build, run, health and service bindings. Both start with version: 3. Root apps use .inferra/app.yaml; monorepos can use api/.inferra/app.yaml and worker/.inferra/app.yaml.
- With no branches map, only the default branch runs. With a nonempty map, list main explicitly if you want it to run. Exact names win, then the longest pattern; equal-length matches fail. feature/* does not match feature/team/login. Pattern TTL counts from the last accepted push.
- Account services use services/*.yaml at the root of the private GitHub <account>/.inferra repository. Grant the App access. Optional account.yaml sets all three quota values and lists every connected repo with all three quota values. An admin merges account service changes first, then app teams add bindings by name and access in app.yaml.
- Attached previews share service data. Create a separately named service for isolated preview data. data: shared is not available yet and does not provide isolation. Removing a branch does not delete account-owned managed services.
- Declare only secret names in YAML. Set values in the dashboard or pipe them to inferra secrets set APP NAME; optionally sync selected GitHub secrets. Never commit values. GitHub-managed secrets are read-only in Inferra; remove from the current owner before transferring ownership.
- Workers use type: worker without an HTTP port or health check. Scheduled jobs use type: job with schedule. Custom image services are not available yet. Native databases are rolling out; confirm availability before depending on them.

## Trial and Paid
- Trial: $15 credit or 14 days, whichever comes first. Card required; Stripe verifies it without charging. One trial per card. Unused credit expires. Apps on Spot; native Postgres, native Valkey and S3 buckets allowed, no other AWS services. A trial change is refused only if it would use remaining credit in under a day.
- At trial end apps stop and native services scale to zero. Data, config and URLs are kept for 30 days; subscribing within that window resumes automatically. Then everything is deleted; repo config is never touched.
- Paid: $25/month including $25 of usage. Extra usage is additional; unused included usage does not roll over. Paid starts on the subscribe date with full charge and included usage; trial credit is dropped. No annual billing. USA customers only for now.
- Native usage is priced per resource, per hour. Production on-demand: $20/vCPU-month, $10/GiB-month memory, $0.15/GiB-month disk. Development Spot apps: $10/vCPU-month and $5/GiB-month memory; disk stays $0.15/GiB-month. Development on-demand uses production rates. Native databases are billed once per service file at on-demand rates, regardless of attached branches. AWS services are priced separately; SQS and DynamoDB on-demand are coming soon, not sold yet.
- Example: 1 vCPU and 2 GiB production app uses $40/month before disk; Paid total is $40. $18 usage costs $25. The calculators show native production estimates and the $25 minimum, not AWS service prices.
- Extra usage charged mid-month and at month-end; month-end includes the next $25 subscription payment in the same card charge. $100 unbilled total triggers an immediate charge at most once a day, settling everything unbilled. Threshold locked for 3 months, then support can arrange a change. It is not a YAML setting.
- Separate $100/day UTC usage cap; no monthly spending limit. Running apps keep running at the cap. New apps, services and cost-adding changes are blocked, and metered AWS access pauses until 00:00 UTC.
- Failed payment: days 0–7 keep running while retried; no cost-adding changes. Emails on days 0, 3, 6. Day 8 apps stop; RDS and ElastiCache snapshotted then deleted; RabbitMQ/Kafka deleted with messages lost; S3/SQS/DynamoDB/native disks kept. Paying during days 8–30 restores databases from snapshots and recreates RabbitMQ/Kafka empty. Everything deleted day 30; warning emails 7 days and 1 day before.
- Cancel: runs to paid month end, then 30-day hold, then deletion. No refunds for used usage. $25 refunded on request within 7 days if usage under $5. A dispute stops the account.

## Help and references

## Website page content


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/setup/

Inferra · Guide

Deploy your first app with config v3

Connect GitHub, add repo.yaml and app.yaml, set secrets and push. Add account services separately when you need them.

1. Prepare your repository

You need a GitHub repository you can push to and a repository admin who can install the Inferra GitHub App. An organization owner may need to approve it. A root app is supported; a monorepo can use api/ and worker/ folders.

Start with $15 of trial credit or 14 days, whichever comes first. Card required; one trial per card. Paid is $25/month including $25 of usage. Usage beyond that is extra; unused included usage does not roll over. Available to USA customers only for now.

Please install the Inferra GitHub App on OWNER/REPO:
https://api.inferralab.com/v1/github/install
Please grant our GitHub team developer access in .inferra/repo.yaml.
Setup guide: https://inferralab.com/setup/

2. Connect GitHub; optionally install the CLI

Install the GitHub App and choose the app repository. The CLI is optional for your first deployment: you can write the files below and use the dashboard. To use it, follow the download instructions, sign in to the dashboard, create a personal token in Settings → Tokens and paste it at the prompt:

inferra login --api https://api.inferralab.com

This is also the CLI’s default API address. An older saved login or INFERRA_API can override it. Never pass a token value as a command-line argument.

3. Add your app and config v3 files

For an existing app, inferra init writes v3: .inferra/repo.yaml, the app folder’s .inferra/app.yaml, and an optional GitHub environment-sync workflow. For api/, run inferra init --app-dir api. It does not create account.yaml. Review generated files before committing. Alternatively, use this complete small Node example.

Create api/package.json:

{"name":"first-app","version":"1.0.0","private":true,"scripts":{"start":"node server.js"}}

Create api/server.js:

const http = require('node:http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' });
  res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true }));
}).listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0');

Create .inferra/repo.yaml on the default branch. For the smallest setup:

version: 3

Create api/.inferra/app.yaml:

version: 3
name: api
type: web
port: 3000
health:
  path: /health

Buildpacks detect Node from package.json. This server answers /health with HTTP 200. Only the default branch runs with the minimal repo file. For a root app, put the app file at .inferra/app.yaml. Download the v3 repo starter.

4. Set secrets safely

Declare runtime secret names in repo.yaml or app.yaml; keep values out of Git. For example, add this to the app file:

secrets: [API_KEY]

Set the value in the dashboard or pipe it to the CLI:

printf %s "$API_KEY" | inferra secrets set api API_KEY

For optional GitHub sync, create GitHub Environments named after deployed branches, such as main and feature/login. The App cannot read GitHub secret values. Generate a workflow that sends only the selected secrets:

inferra init --workflow-only --force --secret API_KEY

Review the workflow before replacing one. Check that it targets https://api.inferralab.com. Each secret has one owner: GitHub-synced values are read-only in Inferra, and the workflow cannot overwrite Inferra-owned secrets. Remove a secret from its current owner before moving it. Missing values leave deployment waiting until supplied. Ordinary values resolve from repo env, repo branch env, app env, then app branch env, with later values winning.

5. Commit and push

For a default branch named main:

git add api/package.json api/server.js .inferra/repo.yaml api/.inferra/app.yaml
git commit -m "Configure Inferra app"
git push -u origin main

Repo rules come from the default branch. App settings come from the branch being deployed.

6. Check deployment and open the app

On GitHub, read inferra/config and inferra/deploy/api separately. Valid configuration does not mean the build is live. Use the dashboard’s app page for its address and deployment progress, or inspect it with the CLI:

inferra orgs
inferra target YOUR_ORG/main
inferra apps status api
inferra deployments api
inferra logs api --follow

Use the repository name shown by inferra orgs for YOUR_ORG.

7. Add account services

For account services, create a private GitHub repository named exactly <account>/.inferra and grant the Inferra GitHub App access. Put account.yaml and services/*.yaml at its root, not inside another .inferra directory. account.yaml is optional for a service-only setup. If present, list every connected app repository and provide all three quota values for the account and each repo.

For a Paid account, create services/orders.yaml in that private repository. This example attaches to application repository shop on main; replace both names with yours.

version: 3
name: orders
type: postgres
hosting: managed
size: db.t4g.micro
storage: 20Gi
engine_version: "17"
attach:
  shop:
    branches: [main]

Have a GitHub admin of the private account repository merge the service change first. Then add the binding to api/.inferra/app.yaml in the application repository:

version: 3
name: api
type: web
port: 3000
health:
  path: /health
services:
  orders: readwrite

Inferra supplies ORDERS_URL to the bound app. Never commit passwords. A binding grants access to an existing attached service; it does not create one. Multiple attached branches share the same data. For separate preview data, create a separately named service and attach it only to previews; data: shared does not create isolated data and is not available yet.

Trial accounts can use native Postgres, native Valkey and S3 buckets, but cannot use managed RDS. Native databases are rolling out; confirm availability with support@inferralab.com before depending on them. Custom image services are not available yet. SQS and DynamoDB on-demand are coming soon.

Previews and workers

To run previews, replace the minimal repo file with this, using your actual default branch name:

version: 3
branches:
  main: {}
  "feature/*":
    ttl: 7d
    quota: {cpu: 0.5, memory: 1Gi, storage: 2Gi}

A nonempty branches map must include the default branch if you want it to run. feature/* matches feature/login, but not feature/team/login. Preview apps have separate spaces; attached account services can share production data. Each preview adds usage and can exhaust trial credit faster. TTL expires a preview 7 days after its last accepted push. Branch removal does not delete account-owned managed services.

For a worker, create worker/.inferra/app.yaml with version: 3, type: worker and process: worker; omit HTTP port and health settings. See the v3 reference and billing.

Troubleshooting

No deploy? Check GitHub App access, accepted repo rules on the default branch and a matching branch entry. Invalid config? Read the named field in the commit status; unknown fields fail validation. Missing secrets? Supply each value through its owner. Failed health check? Check logs, the start command, 0.0.0.0 listener, PORT and health path. Quota or billing rejection? Review repo quotas and account billing. For help or restore requests, email support@inferralab.com.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/org-yaml/

Inferra · Guide

Configuration v3: repo, app and account files

Configure branches in repo.yaml, apps in app.yaml and account services in a private account repository.

Where each file lives

Use config v3 for new deployments. Put .inferra/repo.yaml in the application repository and <folder>/.inferra/app.yaml in each app folder. A root app uses .inferra/app.yaml.

For account services, create a private GitHub repository named exactly <account>/.inferra and grant the Inferra GitHub App access. Put account.yaml and services/*.yaml at its root, not inside another .inferra directory. account.yaml is optional for a service-only setup. If present, list every connected app repository and provide all three quota values for the account and each repo.

A working web app

For repository shop, put this in .inferra/repo.yaml:

version: 3

Put this in api/.inferra/app.yaml. The app must listen on 0.0.0.0:3000 and answer /health:

version: 3
name: api
type: web
port: 3000
health:
  path: /health

Only the default branch runs. CPU defaults to 0.25 vCPU, memory to 256Mi and instances to 1. inferra init --app-dir api generates v3 files and an optional environment workflow; it never writes account.yaml.

Account settings

Example account.yaml at the root of the private <account>/.inferra repository:

version: 3
quota: {cpu: 4, memory: 8Gi, storage: 20Gi}
repos:
  shop:
    quota: {cpu: 4, memory: 8Gi, storage: 20Gi}

Only GitHub admins of that private repository can apply account and service changes. Pull requests validate proposals; an admin’s default-branch merge applies them. Keep secret values out of account settings.

Repository branches and previews

Repo rules are read from the application repository’s default branch for all deployments. To enable previews as well as main:

version: 3
branches:
  main: {}
  "feature/*":
    ttl: 7d
    quota: {cpu: 0.5, memory: 1Gi, storage: 2Gi}

With no branches map, only the default branch runs. With a nonempty map, only listed names and matching patterns run. An exact name wins; otherwise the longest pattern wins. Equal-length matches fail. A * does not cross a slash. TTL is allowed only on pattern keys and counts from the last accepted push. Branch deletion removes its apps and space, but does not delete account-owned managed services.

App settings and overrides

App files are read from the deployed branch. Keep the same app paths on deployed branches. Set CPU, memory and fixed instances directly in app.yaml; use type: worker for continuous work without a public URL, or type: job with a schedule for cron. Workers and jobs have no HTTP port or health check.

version: 3
type: worker
process: worker
cpu: 0.25
memory: 256Mi
instances: 1

Use app branches: entries with the same resolved branch keys as repo.yaml. Maps merge, scalars and lists replace, and null removes a key. App overrides do not stack across multiple matching patterns.

Account services and bindings

For account services, create a private GitHub repository named exactly <account>/.inferra and grant the Inferra GitHub App access. Put account.yaml and services/*.yaml at its root, not inside another .inferra directory. account.yaml is optional for a service-only setup. If present, list every connected app repository and provide all three quota values for the account and each repo.

For a Paid account, create services/orders.yaml in that private repository. This example attaches to application repository shop on main; replace both names with yours.

version: 3
name: orders
type: postgres
hosting: managed
size: db.t4g.micro
storage: 20Gi
engine_version: "17"
attach:
  shop:
    branches: [main]

Have a GitHub admin of the private account repository merge the service change first. Then add the binding to api/.inferra/app.yaml in the application repository:

version: 3
name: api
type: web
port: 3000
health:
  path: /health
services:
  orders: readwrite

Inferra supplies ORDERS_URL to the bound app. Never commit passwords. A binding grants access to an existing attached service; it does not create one. Multiple attached branches share the same data. For separate preview data, create a separately named service and attach it only to previews; data: shared does not create isolated data and is not available yet.

Trial accounts can use native Postgres, native Valkey and S3 buckets, but cannot use managed RDS. Native databases are rolling out; confirm availability with support@inferralab.com before depending on them. Custom image services are not available yet. SQS and DynamoDB on-demand are coming soon.

Quotas and billing

Branch quota entries in repo.yaml require cpu, memory and storage together. Exact branch quotas must fit the repo allocation when account.yaml exists. Pattern quotas apply to each matching preview. Quotas control resources; they are not a monthly spending limit. Start with $15 of trial credit or 14 days, whichever comes first. Card required; one trial per card. Paid is $25/month including $25 of usage. Usage beyond that is extra; unused included usage does not roll over.

Read billing, daily caps and payment timing. Do not rely on usage_budget to stop spending.

Environment, secrets and validation

Put ordinary values under env and only secret names under secrets. Later values win in this order: repo env, repo branch env, app env, app branch env. Repo secret names combine with the effective app list; app overrides replace the app list. Set values with inferra secrets set APP NAME or the dashboard, or explicitly sync them from GitHub. Never override PORT, INFERRA_ or KUBERNETES_ names, or generated service connection variables.

Unknown fields fail validation. GitHub shows inferra/account-config for account changes, inferra/config for app repositories and inferra/deploy/<app> for deployment. An invalid replacement keeps the last accepted configuration. A successful parse alone does not prove every optional feature is available.

Existing repositories

Back up data and review the migration instructions before switching an existing deployment. inferra init --migrate --account ACCOUNT --repo REPO is the migration entry point; inspect its output before merging. Changing files or bindings does not copy data. Create replacements, copy and verify data, switch bindings, then remove old services. Unbind apps before removing an account service file. For migration or restore help, email support@inferralab.com.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/billing/

Inferra · Guide

Trial, Paid and resource quotas

Start with $15 credit for up to 14 days, card required. Paid is $25/month including $25 of usage; additional usage is billed during the month.

Trial

Start with $15 of trial credit or 14 days, whichever comes first. Card required; one trial per card. Stripe verifies your card without charging it. Unused trial credit expires. Trial apps use Spot machines. You can run apps, native Postgres, native Valkey and S3 buckets; no other AWS services.

Native databases are rolling out. Confirm availability with support@inferralab.com before relying on them. A trial change is refused only if it would use the remaining credit in under a day.

When the trial ends, apps stop and native services scale to zero. Data, config and URLs are kept for 30 days. Subscribe to Paid within that window and everything resumes automatically. After 30 days everything is deleted; your repository config is never changed.

Paid: $25/month including $25 of usage

Paid is $25/month including $25 of usage. Usage beyond that is extra; unused included usage does not roll over. The paid month starts when you subscribe, with the full $25 charge and full $25 of included usage. Any trial credit is dropped. No annual billing. Available to USA customers only for now.

Production: $20/vCPU-month, $10/GiB-month memory and $0.15/GiB-month disk. Development apps on Spot: $10/vCPU-month and $5/GiB-month memory; disk stays $0.15/GiB-month. Usage is priced per resource, per hour.

Development branches can opt into on-demand machines at production rates. Native databases are charged once per service file at on-demand rates, however many branches attach. AWS service prices are shown separately; SQS and DynamoDB on-demand are coming soon and are not sold yet.

Example: 1 vCPU and 2 GiB memory running for a full production month uses $40 before disk. Your $25 includes $25 of that usage, so the total is $40. With $18 of usage, you pay $25. A development Spot app at 1 vCPU and 2 GiB uses $20 before disk.

When your card is charged

Usage beyond the included $25 is billed mid-month and at month-end. The month-end charge includes the next $25 subscription payment as a separate line in the same card charge. Your billing month runs from your subscribe date, not the calendar month.

If the unbilled total since the last charge reaches $100, it is charged immediately, at most once a day. Every charge settles everything unbilled up to that moment. The $100 threshold is locked for the first 3 months; after that, only support can arrange a change. It is not a YAML setting.

Daily usage cap

There is no monthly spending limit. The default daily usage cap is $100 per UTC day. At the cap, running apps keep running, but new apps, new services and cost-adding changes are blocked; metered AWS access pauses for the rest of the day. The cap resets at 00:00 UTC. For a higher cap, email support@inferralab.com. The daily cap and the $100 unbilled charge threshold are separate controls.

If a payment fails

On days 0–7, payments are retried and everything keeps running, but cost-adding changes are refused. Emails are sent on days 0, 3 and 6. On day 8, apps stop. RDS and ElastiCache are snapshotted and deleted; RabbitMQ and Kafka are deleted and their messages are lost. S3, SQS, DynamoDB and native disks are kept.

Paying during days 8–30 restores service automatically: databases from snapshots, RabbitMQ and Kafka recreated empty. Everything is deleted on day 30. The dashboard shows the deletion date; reminder emails go out 7 days and 1 day before.

Cancellation and refunds

Cancel and service runs until the end of the paid month, followed by a 30-day hold and then deletion. Export your data before the hold ends. Usage already used is not refundable. The $25 subscription payment is refundable on request within 7 days if usage was under $5. A card dispute stops the account. For cancellation, payment details, invoices or a refund, use Account → Billing or email support@inferralab.com.

Resource quotas are separate

Set branch resource quotas in .inferra/repo.yaml; set account and repo allocations in account.yaml at the root of the private <account>/.inferra repository. Provide cpu, memory and storage together. Quotas are resource limits, not charges or a monthly budget. Each preview adds usage. Account services shared by previews are charged once per service file and share data.

Check usage and deployment

Review account usage and billing in the dashboard. Use inferra usage for resource usage and inferra deployments APP for deployment progress. See pricing and setup.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/cli/

Inferra · Documentation

CLI reference

Commands and flags as printed by the CLI, grouped by task.

Start here

GitHub pushes deploy source. The CLI inspects apps and operates running workloads. Choose a target with inferra target ORG/SPACE; use --org and --space to override it for one command. Commands also accept the global flags printed below.

inferra login
inferra target shop/main
inferra apps
inferra logs api --follow

Use config v3 for new repositories. inferra init generates repo.yaml, app.yaml and an optional environment-sync workflow. Services live in the private account repository. See configuration v3 and Trial and Paid billing. Use inferra COMMAND --help for the flags in your installed version.

Init writes config v3

Run inferra init for a root app, or inferra init --app-dir api for an app folder. It writes .inferra/repo.yaml, the folder’s .inferra/app.yaml and .github/workflows/inferra-env.yml. Both YAML config files use version: 3. Only selected branches run. It does not write account.yaml; that belongs at the root of the private <account>/.inferra repository. Services use services/*.yaml there. --workflow-only uses the existing v3 repo file.

Command list and global flags

Login, targeting and repository setup

Inspect accounts, orgs and apps

Operate workloads and inspect configuration

Logs and metrics

Services and buildpacks

Help, completion and version

Staff commands

Command list and global flags

inferra

Find the available commands and global flags.

$ inferra --help
Inferra deploys repositories connected through the Inferra GitHub App.
Use the CLI to inspect apps and operate running workloads.
Start with: inferra init, commit the generated files, and push to GitHub.

Usage:
  inferra [command]

Available Commands:
  account     Show an account's orgs and pooled resource usage
  accounts    List GitHub accounts and their shared resource usage
  admin       Operator commands for Inferra staff (super admins)
  apps        List apps in the targeted space
  buildpacks  List curated buildpacks
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  db          Inspect managed databases
  deployments Show an app's deployment history (newest first)
  env         List an app's environment variables
  events      Show the org's audit log (who did what)
  exec        Run a command in a running app instance
  help        Help about any command
  init        Create starter Inferra repository configuration
  instances   Show an app's running instances
  invitations List and answer org join requests
  login       Log in with a personal token from the web UI (like cf login)
  logout      Remove the saved token from this machine
  logs        Show recent logs, or follow them with -f
  members     List org members and their roles (GitHub admins and configured teams)
  metrics     Show an app's CPU, memory, requests and latency over time
  org         Show an org's plan, quota usage, owners and spaces (like cf org; change plans in the web UI)
  orgs        List your GitHub repository orgs and their plans
  promote     Deploy the exact image running in another space (no rebuild)
  quota       Show one plan's limits (like cf quota)
  quotas      List plans and their quotas (like cf quotas)
  restart     Restart instances with the same image
  rollback    Redeploy an earlier deployment (default: the previous one)
  secrets     List an app's secret names (values are never shown)
  service     Inspect a managed service
  services    List services in the targeted space and the apps using them
  spaces      List the org's spaces
  start       Start a stopped app
  stop        Stop all instances (keeps URL, config and services)
  target      Show or set the org and space that commands act on
  usage       Show the org's quota and current usage
  version     Print the CLI version
  whoami      Show who the current token belongs to and your orgs

Flags:
      --api string     API URL (default from $INFERRA_API, saved login, or https://api.inferralab.com)
  -h, --help           help for inferra
      --json           print machine-readable JSON
      --org string     org (overrides the saved target and $INFERRA_ORG)
      --space string   space (overrides the saved target and $INFERRA_SPACE)

Use "inferra [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Login, targeting and repository setup

inferra login

Log in with a personal token. Sign in at the Inferra web UI with GitHub,

$ inferra login --help
Log in with a personal token. Sign in at the Inferra web UI with GitHub,
generate a token under Settings → Tokens, then paste it here. The token
carries your own roles: you can do exactly what you can do in the UI.

Then pick the org and space to work in, like "cf login": chosen automatically
when there is only one, otherwise from a numbered list (skip with --org and
--space). Pipelines don't log in: set INFERRA_TOKEN (plus INFERRA_ORG and
INFERRA_SPACE) instead.

Usage:
  inferra login [flags]

Examples:
  inferra login                                  # paste the token (hidden) when asked
  printenv INFERRA_NEW_TOKEN | inferra login --token - --org acme --space dev

Avoid --token <value>: it shows up in shell history and process listings.

Flags:
  -h, --help           help for login
      --org string     org to target (skips the prompt)
      --space string   space to target (skips the prompt)
      --token string   personal token; "-" reads it from stdin (preferred over passing the value)

Global Flags:
      --api string   API URL (default from $INFERRA_API, saved login, or https://api.inferralab.com)
      --json         print machine-readable JSON

inferra logout

Remove the saved token from this machine. To stop a token working everywhere, revoke it in the web UI.

$ inferra logout --help
Remove the saved token from this machine. To stop a token working everywhere, revoke it in the web UI.

Usage:
  inferra logout [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for logout

Global Flags:
      --api string     API URL (default from $INFERRA_API, saved login, or https://api.inferralab.com)
      --json           print machine-readable JSON
      --org string     org (overrides the saved target and $INFERRA_ORG)
      --space string   space (overrides the saved target and $INFERRA_SPACE)

Show who the current token belongs to and your orgs

Examples:

inferra init

Detect the app and generate v3 configuration. Files are kept unless replacement is explicitly requested; review all generated changes.

inferra init
inferra init --app-dir api
inferra init --app-dir worker --name worker
inferra init --workflow-only --force --secret API_KEY

Use --path to select a repository folder and --branch to select its default branch key. --account-path reads a local account repository to check whether the app repo is listed, without writing it. Existing older configurations need migration first: inferra init --migrate --account ACCOUNT --repo REPO. Back up data and review the migration before applying it.

SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/operate/

Inferra · Documentation

Operate your apps

Git declares your apps and resources. Use the dashboard and CLI to operate the workloads already running.

Git owns configuration

Change configuration in Git and push. The dashboard and CLI inspect and operate the apps you declared.

Branches, repo teams, shared env and branch resource quotas: .inferra/repo.yaml on the default branch.

Build, run settings, sizing and service bindings: each app folder’s .inferra/app.yaml from the deployed branch.

Account quotas, repo allocations and team defaults: account.yaml at the root of the private <account>/.inferra repository.

Account services: services/*.yaml in that private repository. A GitHub admin must merge changes there.

Secret names belong in repo.yaml or app.yaml. Supply values through the dashboard, inferra secrets set APP NAME or selected-secret GitHub sync. See secret setup.

Choose the app

In the dashboard, open the repository org, its branch space, then the app. CLI examples below use an app folder named api. Set the target first:

inferra login
inferra target shop/main
inferra apps
inferra apps status api

Scale by changing app.yaml

Edit api/.inferra/app.yaml. For a fixed-size app:

version: 3
name: api
type: web
port: 3000
instances: 2
cpu: 0.5
memory: 512Mi

Commit and push the branch. Check its repo.yaml resource quota, account allocation and billing. Inspect the result with inferra instances api. For supported autoscaling, use a scale map instead of instances; request-based scaling with min above zero is not implemented.

Roll back an image

In the app overview, choose Roll back for the previous deployment, or open Deployments and choose Roll back on an earlier deployment that went live.

inferra deployments api
inferra rollback api
inferra rollback api --to DEPLOYMENT_ID

Rollback redeploys the earlier image. It keeps the current runtime configuration, environment and secret values; it does not restore an old configuration or database. The next eligible push deploys from the pushed commit again, subject to build selection and validation.

Promote the tested image

Promotion deploys the same image in another space without rebuilding, using the target app’s environment and secrets. Both spaces must be on the same cluster; the source deployment must have gone live, and you need developer access to both spaces.

The dashboard has Promote from… and Promote source → target controls in the earlier app view. The current tabbed app view does not expose these controls; use the CLI:

inferra promote api --from staging --space main
inferra promote api --from staging --to main --deployment DEPLOYMENT_ID

Restart, stop and start

Use the app header’s Restart or Stop button. A stopped app shows Start. Restart uses the same image. Stop removes running instances while keeping the URL, configuration and services. These operations require developer access.

inferra restart api
inferra stop api
inferra start api

Set secrets and inspect names

Open the app’s Settings tab. Under Secrets, choose Set value for a missing value or Replace for an existing value. The dashboard requests a restart so running instances receive the new value. Declare runtime secret names in repo.yaml or app.yaml. Values are never returned by secret read APIs.

The CLI lists names and can set values from stdin:

inferra env api
inferra env api --reveal
inferra secrets api
printf %s "$API_KEY" | inferra secrets set api API_KEY

--reveal requires developer access and reveals only ordinary environment values. Managed-service connection values remain hidden. Settings lists environment and secret names.

Logs, metrics and exec

Open the app’s Logs or Metrics tab. See Metrics and logs for chart and live-log controls. The current dashboard has no exec terminal; use the CLI to run a command in a ready instance:

inferra logs api --follow
inferra metrics api --since 6h
inferra exec api -- sh
inferra exec api --pod POD_NAME -- printenv PORT

Exec requires developer access. Without --pod, the CLI selects the first ready pod. Read the complete CLI reference.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/security/

Inferra · Guide

Security and data handling

Inferra isolates apps with gVisor, controls network access by space and service binding, and keeps secret values out of read APIs. This page describes the product controls and data retention.

Isolation and builds

Every app, including trial apps, runs isolated with gVisor. Spaces use separate namespaces and network policies. Buildpacks come from a mirrored catalog pinned by digest. Apps build from source with buildpacks, with no Dockerfile option. Every successful build is submitted for vulnerability scanning. A scan may be incomplete or unavailable; check its result before treating an image as scanned.

Build vulnerability scanning

Check the GitHub scan status and its report when available. An incomplete or unavailable scan is not a clean result. App security overrides in config v3 are not applied by the current deployment path; do not rely on YAML declarations alone to enforce a blocking policy.

Keep dependencies current and review the evidence before deployment. Questions about scanning: support@inferralab.com.

Network rules

Traffic

Rule for every app

Inbound

Through Inferra’s HTTPS gateway on port 443, forwarded to the app’s PORT.

Within a space

Apps in the same space can reach each other.

Outbound

Any public port, including external databases, SMTP and APIs. Private ranges and cloud metadata are blocked.

Managed Postgres and cache

Only apps bound to the service can connect.

Buckets

App pod identity grants access; bucket keys are not handed to apps.

Secret values are write-only

Runtime variables and secrets are encrypted in the platform database with AES-GCM. Apps receive a versioned environment; switching versions rolls running instances. The API does not return secret values. Service connection values also stay hidden, including when a developer reveals ordinary environment variables.

The GitHub App reads variables and secret names, not secret values. Values reach Inferra through an explicitly configured environment workflow or a dashboard write. Read the selected-secret workflow before committing a generated workflow. Applications can still print their own secrets; keep credentials out of logs and public issue reports.

Deletion and restore

Account services are separate from app branches. Removing an app binding revokes its access; it does not delete an account-owned managed service. Unbind all apps before removing a service file from the private account repository. Service deletion follows service-specific snapshot and retention rules; do not assume all service types have backups.

Attached previews share the same service data unless you create a separate service for them. Deleting a preview does not delete account-owned managed services. For a restore request, email support@inferralab.com promptly with the service name and time to restore to. Never send credentials.

When the trial ends, apps stop and native services scale to zero. Data, config and URLs are kept for 30 days. Subscribe to Paid within that window to resume automatically. After 30 days everything is deleted; repository config stays untouched.

Cancel and service runs until the end of the paid month, then a 30-day hold, then deletion. Export data before the hold ends. Usage already used is not refundable; request a refund of the $25 within 7 days if usage was under $5. If a card fails, service-specific stop and recovery rules apply; read the payment failure schedule. Removing GitHub App access also triggers cleanup; export your data first.

Report a vulnerability

Use a private GitHub security advisory on inferra-AI/website. If private reporting is unavailable, open an issue asking for a private reporting channel; do not include exploit details, private data or credentials in a public issue.

Inferra does not hold SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification. We do not claim HIPAA certification or a compliance guarantee for your application.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/external/

Inferra · Guide

Connect to external databases and APIs

Your apps can reach databases and APIs anywhere on the public internet. Allowlist our outbound IP addresses, keep credentials in secrets, and connect over verified TLS.

What your app can reach

Apps reach any public address and port, including external databases, SMTP and APIs. Private address ranges and cloud metadata endpoints are blocked, so private networks in your own cloud aren't reachable yet. Custom services that need the internet must declare internet: true.

Allowlist our outbound IP addresses

If your provider asks for an IP allowlist, copy the Outbound IP addresses from the dashboard Help menu or your organization's overview page, run inferra network, or request GET /v1/platform/network. Allowlist every published address.

These addresses are shared by every app on the platform. An allowlist doesn't identify your app, so always require credentials as well.

Keep credentials in secrets

Declare secret names in app.yaml’s secrets and set their values in the dashboard, or send them from GitHub (see setup, step 4). Never commit passwords, keys or connection strings with passwords in them.

TLS certificates

Always connect over TLS with verification on. What you need depends on who signed the database server's certificate.

If your app needs a certificate authority (CA) it doesn't already trust, there are three ways to provide it:

Way

Works today

Use it when

CA file in your repo + an environment variable

Yes

The CA is public (most provider bundles)

CA stored as a secret, written to a file at startup

Yes

You'd rather not commit it, or it rotates often

Paketo ca-certificates buildpack binding

Not yet

Needs secrets mounted as files (planned). The buildpack is already in every build.

Database

Certificate you need

How

Signed by a public authorityNeon, Supabase, MongoDB Atlas, PlanetScale…

None

Turn verification on, for example sslmode=verify-full. The app image already trusts public authorities.

Signed by the provider's own authorityAWS RDS and Aurora, Azure, Google Cloud SQL, self-hosted

The provider's CA certificate (public)

Commit it to your repo and point the client at it.

Checks your app's certificate (mutual TLS)

A client certificate and private key (secret)

Store both as secrets; write them to files at startup.

A provider CA for one connection

certs/rds-global-bundle.pem        # downloaded from the provider
DATABASE_URL=postgres://…?sslmode=verify-full&sslrootcert=certs/rds-global-bundle.pem

Paths are relative to the app folder at runtime. Check the provider's docs for the current bundle and when it rotates.

A provider CA for the whole app

To trust the CA in every library, not just one connection string, set your language's standard variable in app.yaml’s env. The app's files live under /workspace at runtime.

apps:
  api:
    env:
      NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS: /workspace/certs/rds-global-bundle.pem   # Node.js
      # SSL_CERT_FILE: /workspace/certs/bundle.pem                  # Python, Go, Ruby, OpenSSL
      # REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE: /workspace/certs/bundle.pem             # Python requests

SSL_CERT_FILE replaces the default list rather than adding to it, so build that file from the system bundle plus your CA. Java apps import the CA into a truststore at startup instead.

Client certificates (mutual TLS)

The client certificate can be shared, but its private key is a secret: never commit it. Store both as secrets (multi-line values are fine) and write them to owner-only files when the app starts:

umask 077
printf '%s\n' "$DB_CLIENT_CERT" > /tmp/client.crt
printf '%s\n' "$DB_CLIENT_KEY"  > /tmp/client.key
exec npm start   # then use sslcert=/tmp/client.crt&sslkey=/tmp/client.key

Put those lines in a small start script referenced from your Procfile (for example web: sh start.sh). Built-in secrets as files is planned.

A CA kept in a secret

The same pattern works for a CA you store as a secret. export the variable so the app process sees it:

umask 077
printf '%s\n' "$DB_CA_CERT" > /tmp/db-ca.pem
export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/tmp/db-ca.pem
exec npm start

Many clients also accept the CA straight from the environment, with no file, for example Node's ca: process.env.DB_CA_CERT.

Never turn verification off (sslmode=require without a CA, or rejectUnauthorized: false) to make a connection work. The traffic is still encrypted, but anyone in the middle can pretend to be your database.

Coming later

Secrets as files, for certificates and keys.

Private connections to networks in your own cloud.


SOURCE: https://inferralab.com/docs/sso/

Inferra · Guide

Adding SSO to your app

Your app signs its own users in, with any library or identity service you like. Inferra gives it a stable HTTPS address, outbound access to the identity provider, secrets and a shared session store.

What works today

Method

How

OAuth 2.0 / OpenID ConnectGoogle, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, Auth0, GitHub, Keycloak…

Any OIDC library in your app (for example Passport, Spring Security, Authlib, NextAuth), or a hosted service such as Auth0, Clerk or Okta.

SAML 2.0

A SAML library in your app, or an identity service that turns SAML into OpenID Connect for you.

LDAP

LDAPS (port 636) to a directory reachable on the public internet. Private, office-only directories are not reachable yet.

Set it up

1. Register your app with the identity provider

Use your app's address, shown on its commit check and in the dashboard, as the redirect (callback) URL, for example https://YOUR-APP-ADDRESS/auth/callback. Each preview branch has its own address: register the ones you need, or use a separate client for previews.

2. Keep the client ID and secret out of your code

Put the client ID in branch or app env, declare the client secret’s name in secrets, and set its value in the dashboard (or send it from GitHub with inferra init --workflow-only --secret NAME; see setup, step 4). Your app reads both from its environment.

3. Tell your framework it runs behind HTTPS

Inferra's gateway terminates HTTPS and forwards plain HTTP to your app on $PORT, with X-Forwarded-Proto: https. Turn on your framework's "trust proxy" setting so redirect URLs and secure cookies use https://; otherwise the identity provider rejects the callback.

4. Share sessions between instances

With more than one instance, keep sessions in a shared store. Declare a Valkey service in services/*.yaml in your private account repository and bind it in app.yaml, then point your session library at the URL Inferra injects (see the Configuration v3 reference), or use signed, stateless session cookies.

5. SAML certificates and keys

Store the certificate and private key as secrets (multi-line values are fine). If your library needs file paths, write them to a temporary file at startup; first-class secrets-as-files is coming.

Coming later

Secrets as files, for libraries that read certificates and keys from disk.

Protect with SSO: put sign-in in front of an app through configuration, no code, for internal tools. Planned.

Private networking to reach directories inside your own network.

Pricing

Trial, then $25/month including $25 of usage.

Start with $15 of trial credit or 14 days, whichever comes first. Card required; one trial per card. Paid is $25/month including $25 of usage. Additional usage is extra; unused included usage does not roll over.

Stripe verifies your card without charging it. Trial allows apps, native Postgres, native Valkey and S3 buckets; no other AWS services. Native databases are rolling out. Paid starts on your subscribe date with the full $25 charge and included usage; trial credit is dropped. No annual billing.

Refunds

Usage used is not refundable. Request a refund of the $25 within 7 days if usage was under $5. Refund policy →

Charges, caps and retention

Extra usage is billed mid-month and at month-end, with the next $25 subscription payment at month-end in the same card charge. If the unbilled total reaches $100, it is charged immediately, at most once a day. Every charge settles everything unbilled. The threshold is locked for the first 3 months; after that only support can arrange changes.

The $100/day usage cap is separate from the charge threshold. It resets at 00:00 UTC. Running apps keep running at the cap; new cost-adding changes are blocked and metered AWS access pauses. There is no monthly usage limit.

After trial expiry, data, config and URLs are kept for 30 days; subscribe within that window to resume automatically. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the paid month, followed by a 30-day hold, then deletion. If a payment fails, everything runs on days 0–7 while retries occur and cost-adding changes are refused; on day 8 apps stop and service-specific recovery limits apply. Everything is deleted on day 30. Read the complete payment failure terms.

Usage used is not refundable. Request a refund of the $25 within 7 days if usage was under $5. A dispute stops the account. Questions: support@inferralab.com.

Subscription refunds

The $25 subscription payment is refunded on request within 7 days if usage was under $5. Usage already used is not refundable. Unused trial credit expires, and unused included usage does not roll over.

Cancellation

Cancel and service runs until the end of the paid month, then a 30-day hold, then deletion. Export data before the hold ends. Usage already used is not refundable; request a refund of the $25 within 7 days if usage was under $5. To request cancellation or a refund, email support@inferralab.com from your account’s address.

Card disputes

A card dispute stops the account. Contact support@inferralab.com first if a charge looks wrong.

How to ask

Email support@inferralab.com from your account’s address with the payment date. Do not send card details or credentials. See billing for trial expiry and payment failure terms.
